title: Space Complexity Check
description: Distinguish input vs auxiliary space and common allocation patterns.

questions.prompt: Computing the max of an array with only a few scalar variables is typically:

options.text: Zero space because no new array is named

questions.explanation: Only a few scalars means `O(1)` auxiliary space. Input space that already holds the array is usually not counted as extra.

options.text: The same space as in-place mutation

questions.explanation: `map` builds a new array of size `n`, so auxiliary space is `O(n)`. Methods like `slice`, `filter`, and spread also allocate.

questions.prompt: A recursive sum that calls itself once per index for length `n` often costs:

options.text: `O(1)` space because no new arrays are created

questions.explanation: Recursion uses the call stack. A chain of `n` recursive calls often costs `O(n)` space even with no explicit arrays.

questions.prompt: Why is relying on tail-call optimization risky in JavaScript?

options.text: Tail calls are illegal in the language
Engines do not reliably optimize tail calls

questions.explanation: Tail-call optimization is not something you should rely on in JavaScript engines. Prefer iterative forms when depth is linear in `n`.
